newsitem.title: USA: Weyerhaeuser has lower quarter amid difficult markets.
newsitem.headline: Weyerhaeuser has lower quarter amid difficult markets.

text.p: Weyerhaeuser Co. said Tuesday its earnings fell about 85 percent in the first quarter due to difficult markets for its pulp, paper and packing products.
The company reported first quarter net earnings of $21 million, or 10 cents per share, including a 12 cent per share special charge. A year earlier it earned $142 million, or 72 cents per share.
Sales were $2.61 billion compared with $2.60 billion a year earlier.

"Pulp, paper and packaging markets are still difficult, but we are continuing to focus on our business improvement plans, which will strengthen our long-term competitive position," Weyerhaeuser Chief Executive Officer John Creighton Jr said.

Federal Way, Wash.-based Weyerhaeuser was just the latest forest products company to be hit by a tough market. On Monday, Bowater Inc. and Boise Cascade Corp. reported losses for the quarter, while Louisiana-Pacific Corp. reported a profit only because of a one-time gain.
Weyerhaeuser's pulp, paper and packaging segment operating earnings were $6 million for the first quarter, before a special charge, compared with $162 million for the year-ago first quarter, it said.
Strong U.S. lumber prices, however, helped boost operating earnings at its timberlands and wood products segment to $171 million from $152 million, the company said.
Weyerhaeuser's real estate business and financial services earned $6 million in the quarter, compared with $10 million for the same period of last year, it said.
Weyerhaeuser stock was up 75 cents at $43.625 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
